First complete release of the RAG data-quality benchmark (Weeks 1-5).

How corpus defects (near-duplicates, stale copies with flipped findings, broken parsing, chunking) affect retrieval and claim verification on SciFact, for BM25 and dense retrieval and three verifiers (zero-shot Qwen2.5-1.5B, an NLI cross-encoder as released, and the same model fine-tuned on SciFact train), repeated over two corruption seeds and three training seeds.

- Technical report: `report/REPORT.pdf`
- Key findings: top of `README.md`
- All per-claim predictions, corruption manifests and summaries: `results/`
- Figures: `figures/`
- Fine-tuned models: release `models-week3`
- Exact package versions: `requirements.txt`, `requirements-lock.txt`; every experiment can be re-run with the workflows in `.github/workflows/`

SciFact is not redistributed; it is downloaded from its official release.
